messages:
maria.p: Quick sync — need final decisions on how Dedicated burst + autoscale get represented in customer contracts and oncall runbook. Customer asks keep hitting us; want clarity by EOW.
ajay.k: Can we list the concrete knobs we want in the contract? headroom %, burst window, preemption notice, fallback behavior.
lena.s: From ops POV these are critical: cooldown, preemptable flag per pool, and a hard SLA escape hatch (route to hosted). Also need observability: per-tenant queue length, inflight tokens, p99 latency.
tom.r: Sales: customers push for guaranteed burst for x qps for y minutes. They accept preemption only if we promise a fallback model. Need standard language.
priya.m: Proposed contract snippet: "Dedicated Burst: customer is granted N burst-minutes per billing period with best-effort delivery. Bursts may be preempted for platform health; in preemption events Redwood will route to compatible hosted capacity unless customer opts out." Thoughts?
ajay.k: I like the idea but "best-effort" is vague. We should quantify triggers that cause preemption (e.g., cluster occupancy > 95% sustained for 3m OR p99 latency > 2.5x baseline). That way customers can validate incidents.
diego.o: Engineering constraints: we can't promise fallback latency equal to dedicated. Should be explicit: fallback is subject to hosted capacity and may incur additional latency/cost.
lena.s: For oncall: we need an autoscale runbook entry that says when to override autoscale (manual scale up) and when to let preemption happen. Recommend: only on major customers with active incident exec signoff do we manual intervene.
maria.p: OK, that suggests launch criteria: 1) rollout doc + contract template 2) runbook + playbook (oncall + escalation) 3) telemetry dashboards (per-tenant burst usage, queue, p99, fallback counts) 4) billing labels and docs. We need owners.
ajay.k: I'll own runbook/playbook and the autoscale knobs (cooldown, scale-step, max-burst-concurrency).
priya.m: I'll own contract language and legal review. Tom can help customer comms.
tom.r: Happy to. We should prepare a 1-pager for AE's with example scenarios (e.g., customer requests 10k token burst for 10 mins/month).
ajay.k: Decision items to resolve now: a) burst sizing unit (tokens per minute vs concurrent sessions) b) preemption triggers (occupancy vs latency) c) fallback policy (auto route vs opt-in) d) billing during fallback.
diego.o: My tech recs: prefer concurrent session slots + tokens cap. Slots map to GPU capacity easier. Tokens are messy across model sizes.
lena.s: For preemption triggers: occupancy + p99 latency increase both required. Avoid single-metric flip. Example: occupancy > 94% for 5m AND p99 >= 2x baseline for 3m.
priya.m: For billing: fallback should be billed at normal hosted rate and a distinct line item so customers can see charges. Also the contract must state we won't charge burst credits while preempted — otherwise that feels like double-charge.
maria.p: Good point. We should also decide on a carryover policy for unused burst credits. Do we allow small carryover?
ajay.k: Tech complexity for carryover: tracking across months is easy. The policy decision is product-y. Recommend limited carryover (e.g., up to 20% of monthly allotment) to reduce surprises.
tom.r: Sales prefers carryover (helps close deals) but ok with capped carryover.
priya.m: I'll draft contract options: no carryover vs capped carryover. Legal prefers explicit numeric cap.
lena.s: For SLOs: define p99 generation latency target for dedicated baseline and define delta threshold that triggers mitigation. Add synthetic workload that exercises KV cache warmups for accurate baselining.
diego.o: Implementation note: autoscale cooldown should be 30s-2m depending on metric. Quick windows help with bursty spiky traffic. Also need rate-limits inside the pool to prevent noisy neighbors.
ajay.k: We'll expose knobs: max_scale_step, cooldown_seconds, min_headroom_percent, burst_quota_minutes. Default conservative values: max_scale_step=2x, cooldown=45s, min_headroom=10%.
maria.p: Timeline check: Priya + Ajay + Lena deliver drafts by Thu; Legal review Fri; one-pager for sales + rollout checklist Mon. Launch gated on runbook tested in staging and telemetry validated for 48h.
priya.m: Acknowledged. I'll put draft contract language into the shared doc and ping legal.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/runbook-tests at 2025-11-04T02:00:00Z — please confirm owners for post-deploy verification.
ajay.k: I'll be oncall during the test window and will run the autoscale chaos tests.
lena.s: I'll validate dashboards and alerting (queue > threshold alert, fallback count spike alert).
tom.r: I'll prep the AE one-pager and sample negotiation scripts.
maria.p: If we agree, action items: * Priya: contract drafts * Ajay: runbook + autoscale param defaults + staging test plan * Lena: dashboards + alerts * Tom: sales one-pager * Diego: implement slot-based burst accounting prototype. Callout: keep preemption triggers conservative at launch.
priya.m: Will share contract draft by EOD Thu.
ajay.k: I'll drop the runbook link once uploaded.
lena.s: Also adding a small appendix: "manual rollback checklist" — steps to revert pool to pre-burst state and contact list.
maria.p: Appreciate everyone. If nothing else, +1 to proceed with the plan and we'll reconvene after legal review. :thumbsup:
ajay.k: +1
lena.s: +1
tom.r: +1
priya.m: +1
diego.o: +1
